data.assessment: On-time deliveries are 121.8 of 132.2 orders (0.92). Most lateness is A's late pickups (7.8); A never waits on the road yet loses 1352 s to blocking, while C parks on the road a lot, is always on time and collects nearly all sanctions (14.8, mostly from 23.0 release-deadline overstays). The blocking guard fires only 2.8 times at k=3. Road blocking by parked robots, not a shortage of time for the promise, looks like the main cause of A's late pickups, and nothing is left unfinished.

proposals.title: Tighten blocking_guard threshold from 3 to 2 waiting robots
proposals.rationale: Blocked time is 2404 s, with A alone losing 1352 s and missing 7.8 pickup deadlines, while the eviction guard fires only 2.8 times at k=3. Overstaying past hold_limit only adds a Minor penalty and does not move the robot, so eviction at k=2 is the rule lever that actually clears parked robots from intersections. It should cut A's blocked time and late pickups, raising on_time_deliveries and lowering p95_wait_s without touching the customer promise. A should vote yes. C will likely vote no because it gets Major eviction penalties. B, which both parks and is blocked, is uncertain, so the 2-of-3 quorum may not be met.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 2 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
assumptions: Eviction physically moves a parked robot off the node, whereas a release-deadline overstay only adds a penalty.
A's late pickups are caused mainly by blocking from robots parked on the road, not by distance or load.
Two robots waiting behind a parked robot happens often enough at 75 s order intervals for k=2 to make a measurable difference.
unknowns: How often the blocking count reaches 2, and therefore how many extra evictions and Major penalties C and B would receive.
Whether evicted robots then travel extra distance and miss their own deadlines.
B's net utility change, since B both parks and is blocked; this decides the vote.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Fewer late pickups for A as intersections are cleared sooner.

predictions.subject: metric:blocked_s
predictions.note: Parked robots are evicted when two robots wait behind them.

predictions.subject: metric:p95_wait_s
predictions.note: Less blocking shortens real waits, independent of the promise.

predictions.subject: vote:A
predictions.note: A is blocked most and parks least.

predictions.subject: vote:C
predictions.note: C parks most and would absorb most eviction penalties.

predictions.subject: vote:B
predictions.note: Uncertain. B is blocked 849 s but also parks, so its utility could go either way.

proposals.title: Revise pickup promise from 120 s to 150 s (contract)
proposals.rationale: 7.8 of the 10.4 late deliveries are pickup-deadline misses, almost all at A, whose on-time rate (0.84) is the town minimum. Moving the promise to 150 s would likely turn most of these into on-time deliveries (about +5 to +7) without changing robot behaviour. p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished are therefore expected to stay unchanged, but the promise customers receive is looser. All three companies' utilities rise or stay the same, so all should vote yes.

proposals.why_human: This loosens the promise to customers, and customers have no vote. Under K1, the human must review the measured p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished before accepting. The gain in on-time deliveries comes from relabelling late pickups, not from faster service. It would be better decided after seeing whether the rule-level fix (block_k=2) removes the late pickups by actually reducing blocking.
assumptions: Robots do not slow down or change dispatch behaviour when the pickup deadline is longer.
Most of A's late pickups finish between 120 s and 150 s after the order.
unknowns: The distribution of A's actual pickup times beyond 120 s; if many exceed 150 s, the gain is smaller.
Whether a looser deadline changes route or parking choices in the simulator.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Most of the 7.8 pickup misses fall inside the 150 s window.

predictions.subject: metric:p95_wait_s
predictions.note: Real service is unaffected; only the promise changes.

predictions.subject: metric:min_company_on_time_rate@A
predictions.note: A carries nearly all the pickup misses.
